qt: to the Commission Emmanouil Kefalogiannis (PPE) Subject:

The Greek fur industry is an outward-looking production sector with a long tradition, and it is inextricably linked to the economic and social life of Western Macedonia, in particular the regional units of Kastoria, Florina, Kozani and Grevena. The sector supports an important network of medium and small-sized businesses, skilled professionals and family businesses while preserving valuable know-how built up over generations. By way of illustration, according to industry data, the sector comprises 2 000 businesses and employs 35 000 people in the area of Kastoria alone. Keeping production within the EU, where strict standards apply, provides employment and contributes to regional cohesion and competitiveness while preventing the transfer of production and added value to non-EU countries where standards are lower. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What specific measures does it intend to take to support the competitiveness, outwardlooking approach and long-term sustainability of the Greek fur industry?
How does it intend to ensure the preservation of jobs, know-how and the productive in Western Macedonia, a region that is already facing significant economic and development challenges?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.11.2026) The Commission has made competitiveness a key priority of its political agenda. All EU companies will benefit from the EU competitiveness and simplification agenda, although there are no measures specifically designed for the Greek fur industry. Member States may use a variety of measures as well as available EU funds to mitigate significant economic and development challenges at regional level impacting industries, without undermining competition and fundamental economic freedoms. Although not specifically targeted at the fur sector, enterprises in the Region of Western Macedonia may benefit from support under the European Regional Development Fund1 through the ‘Western Macedonia 2021-2027’ Programme, as well as from the Just Transition Fund2 through the ‘Just Development Transition 2021-2027’ Programme. Both programmes have allocated substantial financial resources to support entrepreneurship, business competitiveness and economic diversification in the region. The first calls for proposals have already been launched successfully under both programmes, attracting significant interest and a high number of applications from eligible beneficiaries.
